title: What to Include in a Laser Cutting RFQ
excerpt: A complete request for quotation gets you an accurate price faster. This checklist covers the files and details a laser cutting supplier needs.
meta_title: What to Include in a Laser Cutting RFQ | JASSCO Steel
meta_description: A practical checklist for laser cutting quotations: DXF files, dimensioned drawings, material grade, thickness, edge requirements, tolerances and quantities.
content:
The quickest way to get an accurate laser cutting quotation is to send a complete package the first time. Missing details lead to questions, assumptions and delays. Use this checklist before you send your next request for quotation (RFQ).

1. A clean DXF file for every part

Laser cutting machines are programmed from 2D vector files. Send one DXF per part, drawn at 1:1 scale in millimetres, with closed contours and no duplicate or overlapping lines. Remove title blocks, dimensions and notes from the cutting layer.

2. A dimensioned PDF drawing

The DXF tells the machine what to cut; the drawing tells the supplier what matters. Include the drawing number and revision, critical dimensions and any bends, threads or welds that follow cutting.

3. Material grade and thickness

State the exact grade (for example a specific stainless steel or aluminium alloy) and the thickness. If equivalent grades are acceptable, say so — it can help availability and lead time.

4. Edge, burr and finish requirements

Note any requirements for edge quality, deburring, protective film, or a finish such as powder coating after cutting.

5. Tolerances

Only specify tight tolerances where they are functionally needed. Over-tight general tolerances add cost without adding value.

6. Quantities and order pattern

Give the quantity per batch and the expected annual volume. This determines how parts are nested and whether another process, such as press tooling, may be more economical for high volumes.

7. Delivery, packing and documents

Include the delivery destination, target date, packing requirements and any inspection reports or material certificates you need.

Quick checklist

  • DXF for each part (1:1, mm, closed contours)
  • Dimensioned PDF with revision
  • Material grade and thickness
  • Edge and finish requirements
  • Critical tolerances
  • Batch and annual quantity
  • Delivery location, date and documentation
